transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-18
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Taylor Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Markus Lee (CTO, Praxis Health), Aisha Gomez (Head of Security, Praxis), Daniel Park (Infra Lead, Praxis)

Summary (auto-gen, rough):
Quick walkthrough of Redwood encryption model: at-rest + in-transit encryption, KMS options (hosted KMS vs BYOK), HSM integration possibilities, key rotation, audit logs, and data residency controls. Praxis asked specifics about BYOK + HSM and whether Redwood Dedicated/Private supports FIPS-level HSM connectors. Agreed next steps: share architecture diagram and schedule an on-prem HSM test window.

Topics: encryption at rest; in transit; KMS (AWS/GC/Azure) integration; Bring Your Own Key (BYOK); HSM/Cloud HSM; key rotation & rotation policies; audit logs & retention; SOC 2/ISO alignment; data residency controls

Transcript:
[00:00] Taylor (Redwood AE): ok, good afternoon everyone, uh we'll run through encryption at rest and KMS options, priya will jump into the technical bits — priya, over to you.
[00:18] Priya (Redwood SE): yeah hi all, thanks. So quick agenda, i'll cover in-transit TLS, at-rest encryption, the KMS options we support — native cloud KMS, BYOK flow, and HSM integration — then we'll go into audit logs and rotation.
[00:35] Markus (Praxis): sounds good. for context, our compliance team cares about proving separation of keys and having control of key lifecycle, we also have data residency in eu and us, and we need to validate HSM-backed keys for a pilot.
[00:46] Aisha (Praxis): and i just want to be explicit, SOC2 and ISO 27001 are table stakes; we also need immutable audit logs we can ingest into our splunk.
[00:55] Priya (Praxis): yep, totally understood.
[01:05] Priya: first, in-transit — all traffic to Redwood endpoints is TLS 1.2/1.3, we terminate at the edge and then use mTLS between internal services for Dedicated/Private. For the hosted API we use managed load balancers with certs rotated via our CA process. Sorry if the doc spelled that weirdly earlier, the auto notes sometimes say m-tls as mtls, all that.
[01:30] Daniel (Praxis): can you confirm we can do client cert auth for our service-to-service calls? we prefer cert-based svc auth for prod.
[01:38] Priya: for Private and Dedicated yes — we support client certs and SAML/SSO for user access; for Hosted API we rely on API tokens plus IP allowlists and VPC peering options.
[01:50] Taylor: and to add, for high-security customers we recommend Private deployment where you can plug into your KMS/HSM and your network.
[02:02] Priya: ok at-rest — all persisted data is AES-256 by default. On hosted, keys are managed in the cloud provider KMS (e.g., AWS KMS or GCP KMS).
[02:15] Markus: so hosted uses provider keys — how do you separate tenant keys? i.e., we want dedicated key per tenant so we can revoke or rotate independently.
[02:25] Priya: good q. we do envelope encryption: data keys are generated per-tenant, encrypted with a root key in KMS. For hosted we use customer-scoped keys where possible; for enterprise customers we recommend BYOK.
[02:40] Aisha: BYOK — can you walk through the flow? where do we store the root key, who has access, and how does rotation work?
[02:48] Priya: sure. BYOK flow basically: you provision a key in your cloud KMS or HSM, then you give Redwood a minimal access role to use that key for envelope encryption operations. Redwood never stores the unencrypted root KEK — we only get ciphertext. For on-prem HSMs we support remote signing calls to the HSM via standardized APIs, so Redwood only sees sealed blobs.
[03:10] Markus: so for an HSM-backed key, Redwood would call into our HSM to decrypt data encryption keys on demand? that has perf implications, right?
[03:20] Priya: yes, exactly. To avoid latency, we use caching of unwrapped data keys in memory for a short TTL in the runtime — it's secure and reduces round trips to HSM. We also support pre-warmed key caches for bursty workloads, and we document the TTL and cache invalidation.
[03:40] Daniel: do you support CloudHSM (aws cloudhsm) and external HSM vendors?
[03:45] Priya: we have been tested with AWS CloudHSM and Azure Dedicated HSM; for on-prem HSMs we do a connector pattern — often customers run a small adaptor in their VPC that proxies to their HSM appliance. that's how we did the early Aurora Health POC (i think the notes say aurora but the transcript spelled it differently).
[04:05] Aisha: what's the FIPS posture? we need FIPS 140-2 validated HSM and crypto modules.
[04:11] Priya: Redwood itself runs FIPS-mode cipher suites where required, and for Dedicated/Private deployments we can integrate with FIPS-validated HSMs. We'll need to validate the exact module version; we can share our compatibility matrix.
[04:25] Taylor: quick objection we often hear: "if we hand you access to our KMS, how do we maintain separation of duties?" engineers want to ensure Redwood can't just get raw keys.
[04:36] Priya: right, separation is via roles and restricted IAM policies. For BYOK we ask for a cryptographic usage policy that only allows Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey calls from a specific role. We also support just-signing flows where Redwood gets only signed key material back rather than plaintext.
[04:55] Markus: can you show an example IAM policy?
[04:58] Priya: i'll include the example in the follow-up pack — short snippet, least-privilege role, and a conditional based on source VPC.
[05:08] Speaker 1: uh hm.
[05:12] Daniel: audit logs — we need proof of key usage, e.g., who called decrypt and when; we want to ship those events to our SIEM.
[05:20] Priya: absolutely — we surface detailed audit events for key operations and access to sensitive artifacts. For Hosted we surface anonymized events; for Dedicated/Private we can push full audit logs to a customer S3/ELK target or support push to CloudWatch/Stackdriver. We'll include sample log lines.
[05:40] Aisha: retention policy? we have retention constraints for at least seven years for some records.
[05:45] Priya: our default log retention is configurable; for enterprise contracts we can extend retention and provide exported immutable bundles for audits. We'll note SLA on retention in the security pack.
[06:00] Markus: how do you handle key rotation and re-encryption? we have long-lived datasets, need to rotate root keys without downtime.
[06:09] Priya: we support rotating the KEK — we will generate a new master key and rewrap the data KEKs. For large datasets we do lazy rewrap: existing ciphertext remains valid and is rewrapped on access, background rewrap jobs can be scheduled. This avoids big take-downs.
[06:28] Taylor: i want to flag that rewrap may have cost/latency impact; we can model that in our optimize recommendations.
[06:36] Aisha: are there any scenarios where Redwood holds unencrypted customer data outside our region?
[06:42] Priya: no, data residency controls ensure that persisted data is stored in chosen regions for Private and Dedicated; for Hosted we have region selection and can restrict storage to EU or US regions. We do have cross-region backups optionally, but those are controlled via agreement.
[07:00] Daniel: we saw notes about KV cache and that caching could leak keys if misconfigured — how do you mitigate that?
[07:07] Priya: the KV cache refers to model KV cache not cryptographic keys; cryptographic keys are never persisted on disk. Data encryption keys can be cached in memory only, and we guard the process with mlock to avoid swapping and rotate the cache periodically.
[07:22] Markus: acceptance criteria for our security review: 1) evidence of SOC 2 reports, 2) BYOK flow doc + example IAM, 3) HSM compatibility matrix, 4) audit log export and retention options, 5) penetration test summary.
[07:36] Taylor: we'll deliver SOC 2 + ISO summaries and penetration test high-levels, and priya will get the BYOK + HSM docs.
[07:44] Aisha: on the HSM testing — we want to schedule a short benchmark to measure latency when decrypting data keys via our HSM to verify throughput.
[07:53] Priya: yes we can do a 2-hour bench window; we'll need a test account and some sample payloads. we'll plan for 2026-09-24 unless that conflicts.
[08:03] Daniel: that works for us, i'll coordinate.
[08:08] Markus: are there any edge cases if we use dedicated GPU pools? does the runtime persist any model-related cache to disk that could contain customer data?
[08:18] Priya: the serving runtime stores transient KV cache for models but we treat that as ephemeral and encrypt any persisted artifacts. For Dedicated/Private, you control the disk and can enforce full-disk encryption; Redwood can configure runtime to not persist KV caches across restarts if you want stricter controls.
[08:37] Aisha: can you support customer-managed KMS for signing webhooks or other ephemeral tokens?
[08:43] Priya: yes, we can use your KMS for signing flows; for hosted we might use a proxy key but for Dedicated/Private we call your KMS directly.
[08:52] Speaker 2: mm hmm.
[08:55] Taylor: quick callout on rotation cadence — recommended rotation for master keys is annually, data keys more frequently depending on workload; we'll include recommended policies.
[09:06] Markus: one more question — if we bring our own key and later terminate the contract, what's the revocation process? can we ensure Redwood loses access immediately?
[09:16] Priya: yes — you can revoke the role or disable the key in your KMS; since Redwood only has encrypted blobs, disabling the key prevents decryption. We'll work with you on secure offboarding steps and certificate/key revocation checklist.
[09:30] Aisha: any SLA implications if keys revoked accidentally?
[09:33] Taylor: we'd treat that as customer-managed key availability incident; we have runbooks to work through it but restoring access requires customer action or providing a recovery key per contract. We'll capture expected responsibilities in the contract.
[09:47] Daniel: regarding audit evidence — is there a way to get signed attestations of key operations (like signed audit bundles)?
[09:55] Priya: we can provide signed audit export bundles; for Private deployments you can host the audit store. For hosted accounts we offer signed snapshots on request as part of enterprise agreements.
[10:05] Markus: can we get a mapping of Redwood roles to the data plane access rights? we need least-priv policy mapping for our internal review.
[10:13] Priya: yes, we'll provide a roles->permissions table in the security packet.
[10:18] Taylor: ok let's recap and next steps.
[10:22] Taylor: action items: send SOC2/ISO summaries, BYOK architecture and IAM snippets, HSM compatibility matrix, schedule the 2-hour HSM perf window on 9/24, provide sample audit log lines and retention options.
[10:37] Markus: thanks, that's excellent. we'll follow up with our compliance questionnaire answers and a list of regions.
[10:44] Aisha: thanks everyone.
[10:46] Priya: thanks, i'll send notes and the pack.
[10:49] Taylor: thanks all, bye.
